name: Machine Seated Row
grip: Pronated overhand or neutral grip on machine lever handles.
description: Pull bilateral machine handles horizontally toward the torso while seated with chest supported against a vertical pad, developing upper back and lat thickness without lower back fatigue.
setup: Adjust the seat height so the machine handles align across mid-chest level when gripped.
Adjust the chest support pad forward or backward so you can reach the handles with arms extended without rounding your spine.
Sit firmly with your chest against the pad and feet planted on the foot supports.
Grasp the handles with an overhand or neutral grip.
instructions: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows backward in a horizontal path.
Pull the handles toward your ribcage until elbows pass the torso line, keeping chest firmly against the pad.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together forcefully at peak contraction.
Slowly extend your arms under control, resisting the weight stack until arms are fully extended and back muscles feel a deep stretch before the next rep.
cues: Lead with the elbows, squeeze shoulder blades.
Keep chest glued to the support pad.
Control the stretch on the return.
commonMistakes: Arching backward and pulling the chest off the support pad to jerk the weight.
Shrugging shoulders upward toward the ears.
Shortening the range of motion by stopping short of a full stretch.

variantNote: Bilateral chest-supported machine row. The vertical chest pad stabilizes the torso, eliminating lower back shear stress and preventing cheating.
reviewNotes: Drafted from FitTrack ID 8 (Machine Seated Row).
Distinguished from unilateral plate-loaded row and cable row by selectorized bilateral chest-supported configuration.
